items.description: Sec. V-A says the 'design domain of size 192×64' gives 12,288 pixel design variables and is 'illustrated in Fig. 2B'. The Fig. 2B caption calls that figure a 'Full-view' of the beam and says 'only half of the domain is optimized' by symmetry. The text never says whether 192×64 is the modelled half or the whole beam. The variable count points to the half, and the span is assumed to run along the 192 direction.
readings: 192×64 elements is the modelled symmetric half (span 192 horizontal, height 64), so the full beam is 384×64 (6:1)
192×64 is the full beam (3:1) and the modelled half is 96×64 elements
The whole 192×64 beam is modelled with no symmetry reduction

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption only says 'both lower corners are supported'. Which degrees of freedom are fixed (pin or roller) can only be seen in the figure. Sec. V-A refers to Ref. [35], which is not provided.
readings: Classic MBB: the outer lower corner of the half model is fixed vertically only (roller, u_y = 0), and the symmetry edge stops horizontal motion (full beam: pin + roller or roller + roller)
The outer lower corner is pinned (u_x = u_y = 0), so both lower corners of the full beam are pinned (arch action, no bottom tie needed)

items.entity: symmetry (mid-span) edge of the half model
items.description: The Fig. 2B caption says 'Using symmetry, only half of the domain is optimized'. The text never gives the boundary condition on the cut edge, or says which half (left or right) is modelled.
readings: Left half modelled: u_x = 0 on every node of the left (mid-span) edge, u_y free; load at the top of that edge, support at the bottom-right corner
Right half modelled: mirror image, with u_x = 0 on the right edge and the support at the bottom-left corner
The half design is mirrored and the full beam is analysed with both corner supports (no explicit symmetry condition)

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption puts supports at 'both lower corners' but does not say whether one corner node is held or a short run of bottom-edge nodes.
readings: A single node at the outer bottom corner
A few neighbouring bottom-edge nodes (e.g. 2–3) at the corner

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption says 'A downward force is applied at the center'. It does not say whether this is the top edge at mid-span (classic MBB) or mid-height of the mid-span section. Sec. V-A gives no load location, so the exact point is only in the figure.
readings: Top edge at mid-span (x = 0.5 L_full, y = H); in the half model, the top node of the symmetry edge
Mid-height at mid-span (x = 0.5 L_full, y = 0.5 H); in the half model, the middle node of the symmetry edge

items.description: Neither the Fig. 2B caption nor Sec. V-A says whether the force is a single nodal point load or spread over several nodes or an element edge.
readings: A single nodal point force
The force spread over a few top-edge nodes around mid-span

items.description: No load magnitude is given (Fig. 2B, Sec. V-A, Ref. [35] not provided). The text also doesn't say whether the half model carries the full load or half of it, or whether the reported compliances (246, 270, 394, 735) are for the half model or the full beam.
readings: The half model is loaded with F = 1 at the symmetry node (total load 2 on the full beam)
The full beam is loaded with F = 1, i.e. 0.5 at the symmetry node of the half model

items.description: The solid stiffness and thickness are not given anywhere for the MBB example; Sec. V-A only refers to Ref. [35]. Both scale the reported compliance values.
readings: E0 = 1 with unit thickness (dimensionless)
Physical values, e.g. E0 = 210 GPa with a given thickness (compliance ∝ 1/(E0·t))

items.description: Poisson's ratio is not stated anywhere in the MBB setup (Sec. V-A, Fig. 2B).
Plane stress or plane strain is not stated; Eq. 11 only gives KU = F. Plane strain changes the effective Poisson's ratio.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.description: Eq. 11 uses K(v) for 'density-based topology optimization' but gives no interpolation law or penalty exponent; it refers to Ref. [35].
readings: SIMP with p = 3
SIMP with p = 1 (no penalization)
Penalty continuation, e.g. p raised from 1 to 3

items.description: Eq. 11 allows v_ij = 0, but the minimum stiffness used to keep K non-singular is not given.
readings: Emin = 1e-9·E0
Emin = 1e-3·E0
Emin = 0 with a density lower bound of 1e-3

items.entity: target volume fraction V0 for the 192×64 run
items.description: Sec. V-A only says 'a predefined volume fraction V0'. The value 0.4 appears only for generating the training data (Sec. V-B), and the other values (0.5, 0.3) belong to other resolutions (Sec. VI-E). So 0.4 has to be inferred.
readings: V0 = 0.4 (same as the training-data designs)

items.entity: which density field carries the volume constraint
items.description: Eq. 11 requires V(v) = V0 on the filtered physical density v. Eq. 12 instead enforces V(ṽ) = V0 on the unfiltered field, before the radius-2 cone filter is applied. These differ because the normalised filter does not conserve volume near the edges.
readings: Constraint on the unfiltered design ṽ (Eq. 12)
Constraint on the filtered physical density v (Eq. 11)

items.description: Sec. V-A says 'cone filter with a radius of 2' but gives no units (element widths assumed), exact kernel, or boundary or symmetry-edge treatment; it refers to Ref. [35].
readings: r = 2 element widths, weights max(0, 2 − d), normalised by the local weight sum and truncated at all edges (standard density filter)
r = 2 element widths, zero-padded convolution without renormalising at the edges
r = 2 element widths with mirror padding at the symmetry edge

items.description: The element type and how the FE mesh lines up with the design pixels are not stated; Sec. V-A says the finite-element implementation follows Ref. [35].
readings: One 4-node bilinear square (Q4) element per design pixel (192×64 elements)
A different element type or an FE mesh finer than the design grid (e.g. Q8/Q9)

items.description: No passive solid or void regions are mentioned for the MBB example (Sec. V-A, Fig. 2B); presumably there are none.
readings: None: the whole rectangle can be designed
Small solid non-design pads at the load point and the support corner

items.description: The Fig. 2B caption calls the objective 'elastic compliance (elastic potential energy)', but Eq. 11 minimises UᵀKU (= FᵀU), which is twice the strain energy. This affects the reported numbers (246, 270, etc.).
readings: C = UᵀKU = FᵀU
C = ½UᵀKU (strain energy)

items.entity: optimiser settings for the reference pixel-based run
items.description: Only 'L-BFGS-based topology optimization' is named (Sec. V-B, VI-A, VI-B). The text gives no design parameterisation, starting design, iteration count or stopping rule for the reference run. The training-data runs started from eroded earlier designs.
readings: L-BFGS on pixel logits with the volume-matching sigmoid (Eq. 12) and the cone filter, uniform starting density V0, fixed iteration budget
Standard SIMP with OC/MMA updates on densities from a uniform V0 start until a design-change tolerance is met
